name: Marketplace publication governance - publish nothing without a measured context cost
description: Blueprint 90 of 96 (design BP-REL-04). Publish a skill or plugin only once its licence, its MEASURED per-turn context cost, its default enable scope and its deprecation path are all decided. Mechanism: publication is treated as a CONTRACT WITH CONSUMERS, and the binding step is a measurement - an artifact whose context cost cannot be measured cannot be published, because a consumer cannot budget for an unmeasured tax. The admission decision itself goes to a council rather than to the author, since the author is the party with the least incentive to count the cost.

artifact_path.description: ABSOLUTE path to the skill or plugin being published

target_marketplace.description: The marketplace that will register it. A marketplace with no on-disk source is a dangling reference and is rejected.

licence.description: SPDX identifier or an explicit proprietary statement. There is no default: an unstated licence is a licence question pushed onto every consumer.

declared_context_cost_tokens.description: The per-turn cost the publisher CLAIMS. It is compared against a measurement; a mismatch beyond tolerance blocks publication.

cost_tolerance_ratio.description: Allowed |measured - declared| / measured before the declaration counts as wrong

default_enable_scope.description: USER scope only. A project-scope default returns the moment a consumer changes cwd, which is why disabling at project scope was never a durable cure.

ships_hooks.description: Whether the artifact carries hooks. A published artifact that ships hooks is an execution surface for every consumer and must say so prominently.

deprecation_policy.description: How this artifact will be RETIRED, written before it is published. A retired artifact must be DEREGISTERED, not merely disabled.

publication-author.description: Prepares the manifest, the licence declaration and the deprecation plan

cost-measurer.description: Measures the per-turn context cost the artifact imposes on a consumer, independently of the author's estimate

governance-council-member.description: A council seat on the admission decision - is this worth publishing at all, given that every published artifact taxes its consumers?

owner.description: The human owner - decides which internal artifacts are worth publishing at all

routes.reason: at least one council seat must be cross-vendor or the admission vote inherits one vendor's blind spot about its own ecosystem

licence-declared.expression: licence_declared == true AND licence_in_allowlist == true AND obligations_enumerated == true

user-scope-and-deprecation.expression: default_enable_scope == user AND deprecation_path_written == true AND deregistration_step_present == true

work_unit.title: Declare the artifact licence and enumerate every obligation it imposes on a consumer
work_unit.question_or_target: State the licence and enumerate its obligations for a CONSUMER (attribution, share-alike, field-of-use restrictions, ML-training riders). Check every vendored dependency inside the artifact for a licence that is stricter than the declared one - the strictest inherited term governs.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: reading obligations out of licence text and reconciling inherited terms is substantive

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per obligation the licence clause it comes from, and for each vendored dependency its own licence with the file the notice was read from; this is a licence RECORD, not legal advice, and must say so
tests_required: a vendored dependency under a stricter licence must force the declared licence to the stricter term or FAIL the stage
an artifact with no licence file must FAIL rather than default to permissive
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reader who spot-checks at least one obligation against the quoted clause
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9001 emitted only when the licence is declared, obligations are enumerated with clause anchors, and every vendored dependency is accounted for; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9001 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry on a missing licence file - that is an authoring gap the publisher must close, not a transient failure

stages.title: No publication without an enumerated licence
Measure what a consumer will pay per turn

work_unit.title: Measure the per-turn context cost the artifact imposes when enabled, and compare it to the declaration
work_unit.question_or_target: Measure the artifact's contribution to a consumer's per-turn context: its always-loaded surface (description, frontmatter, tool schemas) as distinct from its lazily-loaded body. Compare the measurement to declared_context_cost_tokens and compute the deviation ratio.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: independent of the author, because the author's declaration is the thing under test

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the token count with the tokeniser named, split into always-loaded and lazily-loaded, plus the deviation from the declaration; a single total with no split hides whether the cost is paid every turn or only on use
tests_required: an artifact whose always-loaded surface is measured must produce a NON-ZERO always-loaded figure; a zero there means the measurement missed the description and frontmatter
both-states control: measuring with the artifact enabled and disabled must produce DIFFERENT totals - if they match, the instrument is not seeing the artifact at all
a declaration outside tolerance must FAIL the gate rather than be silently corrected
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the admission council reads the measurement; the author may not revise the declaration after seeing it without recording that it was revised
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9002 emitted only when the enabled/disabled control shows a difference AND the always-loaded split is non-zero; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9002 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry with a different tokeniser if the first measurement returns zero; a second zero means the instrument is blind and the artifact must not be published

stages.title: An unmeasured artifact cannot be budgeted by a consumer
The retirement plan is written BEFORE publication

work_unit.title: Write the deprecation path, including the DEREGISTRATION step
work_unit.question_or_target: Write how this artifact is retired: the signal that retirement is due, the migration a consumer must make, and the explicit DEREGISTRATION step. Disabling is not retiring - a declared-RETIRED artifact that stays registered is still a live reference in every consumer's catalogue.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: designing a migration path for unknown future consumers is judgement

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the manifest with licence, measured cost split, enable scope, hook disclosure, and a deprecation section containing a named deregistration step; a deprecation section without deregistration is the measured failure mode
tests_required: a manifest whose deprecation section lacks a deregistration step must FAIL
an artifact with ships_hooks true whose manifest does not disclose the execution surface must FAIL
default_enable_scope project must FAIL - it returns when the consumer changes cwd
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the admission council reviews the manifest as a whole before the vote
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPW-9003 emitted only when the manifest carries licence, measured cost, USER enable scope, hook disclosure and a deregistration step; otherwise FAILED:BPW-9003 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: one retry after adding the missing manifest section; a second failure means the policy input itself is incomplete and returns to the publisher

stages.title: USER scope, with a deregistration step
A published artifact that ships hooks is an execution surface
Is this worth publishing at all?
Publication is an owner call - every published artifact taxes its consumers
stages.prompt: Licence enumerated, context cost measured against the declaration, USER enable scope, hook surface disclosed, deprecation path written with a deregistration step, council advised. Publish, publish narrowed, or keep private?

estimate.measurement_source: 09-WORKFLOW-BLUEPRINT-LIBRARY.md#BP-REL-04 - the catalogue-tax measurement (98 installed / 9 enabled, two orphaned marketplace clones on disk, one unregistered clone shipping hooks, and a declared-RETIRED marketplace still registered)

impact.blast_radius: a published artifact propagates to every consumer of the marketplace; unpublishing does not retract copies already installed, which is why the deprecation path is written before publication rather than after

derived_from.credit: owner - install-means-enabled-by-default and the USER-scope cure

rollback_to: a plain marketplace registration with no governance record

x_extensions.mechanism: publication is blocked on a MEASUREMENT, not on a declaration: the always-loaded context cost is measured with an enabled/disabled control and compared to the publisher's claim within a tolerance. The admission vote sits with a cross-vendor council because the author is the party least motivated to count the tax it imposes.
x_extensions.council_preset_available: platform/council/presets/C-H60-marketplace-plugin-admission.councilspec.json - the program already designed a marketplace-plugin-admission preset; the council stage here references the CouncilSpec CONTRACT (the schema), and a runner should bind that preset as the concrete seat allocation.

not_a_duplicate_because.vs_skill-plugin-portfolio-stocktake: that is the CONSUMER side - it prunes what is already installed against a context budget. This is the PUBLISHER side and it runs once, before an artifact exists in anyone's catalogue.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_license-and-rights-governance-registe: a licence register records rights across a corpus; this gates ONE publication on four coupled preconditions of which licence is only the first, and its binding step is a cost measurement rather than a rights record.
not_a_duplicate_because.vs_pr-shepherd-to-merge: that lands code into a repo; this admits an artifact into a catalogue that other consumers load every turn

contraindications: NOT for a private one-off skill only this estate uses - though the licence and scope questions still apply
NOT for republishing an unchanged artifact - the cost measurement is the expensive part and it is keyed to the artifact's content

benchmark_cases.given: an artifact published with a declared per-turn cost
benchmark_cases.expect: a consumer's measured cost matches the declaration within cost_tolerance_ratio

benchmark_cases.given: the cost instrument run with the artifact enabled and disabled
benchmark_cases.expect: DIFFERENT totals - identical totals mean the instrument cannot see the artifact
it is DEREGISTERED, not merely disabled - the measured failure mode is a declared-RETIRED marketplace that stayed registered

params.deprecation_policy: Retire when CrossHair supports the language surface natively; migration is to call the tool directly; the deregistration step removes the marketplace entry, not merely the enable flag.

worked_examples.note: The declaration (300) was close but not exact; 268 measured is a 11.9% deviation, inside the 20% tolerance. Publishing on the DECLARED figure alone would have shipped a number nobody had counted - which is how a catalogue accumulates 98 installed artifacts and no budget.

x_extensions.owner_decision: YES - which internal skills are worth publishing at all, given that every published artifact adds catalogue tax for its consumers. Represented as the owner-publication-decision human checkpoint with a publish-narrowed option, so 'split it so consumers can enable only what they need' is a first-class outcome rather than an afterthought.
unverified: That a consumer's measured per-turn cost will match this workflow's measurement is UNVERIFIED - the measurement is taken on the publisher's box with the publisher's tokeniser. Settling experiment = the declared-vs-measured benchmark run by an actual consumer after publication; a systematic gap would mean the instrument, not the declaration, needs fixing.

The catalogue-tax figures (98 installed / 9 enabled) are quoted from the design card and are NOT re-measured here. Settling experiment = audit the currently-registered marketplaces and count how many have a source on disk and a declared licence.
